A query keeps its slot until its answer body is read, and a waiting query takes the slot of the query that ends.
The read service still retries an error 202 that another client causes.
Each query carries the signal of the HTTP request that asked for it, joined with the read service's timeout.
When the request ends early, a waiting query leaves the queue and rejects with the reason of the signal.
A running query stops too: its HTTP request to ClickHouse aborts, and ClickHouse cancels the query.
